# T12 — Save and load

**Depends on:** T04, T10, T11
**Spec:** DESIGN.md §0, §8.1–§8.4
**Phase:** 3

## Goal

`src/game/save.ts`. Survive a page reload mid-run, and never show an enemy in a place the seed
would not put it.

## The central design choice

**The map is not saved.** DESIGN.md §0 guarantees it can be regenerated byte-identically from
`(seed, level, generator, attempt)`, so persisting it would be redundant state that can only
drift out of sync with the board.

This is only sound because the global RNG is consumed by *nothing but* level construction. If
a single combat roll ever touched the global RNG, a regenerated level would place enemies
differently from the one the player left, and every save would quietly lie. T20 is the test that
keeps this honest.

What *does* need saving is the gameplay RNG state, because combat rolls genuinely advance it.
That is 4 numbers, and it is what makes a resumed run roll the same dice as an uninterrupted
one.

## What to build

### 1. Keys (DESIGN.md §8.1)

| Key | Contents |
|---|---|
| `netdev_save_v1` | At most one in-progress run, or absent |
| `netdev_history_v1` | Run history, newest 50 |

### 2. The schema (DESIGN.md §8.2)

```ts
interface SaveFile {
  version: 1;
  seed: string;
  level: number;
  turnCount: number;
  player: SerializedEntity;
  inventory: InventoryEntry[];
  entities: SerializedEntity[];
  explored: string;                              // base64 of a Uint8Array(60*25)
  playRngState: [number, number, number, number];
  generator: "digger" | "digger-retry" | "uniform";
  attempt: number;
  savedAt: string;                               // ISO 8601, display only
}
```

`entities` holds **enemies, floor items, and corpses** — everything mutable. Note it does *not*
hold the player, who has their own field.

`explored` is base64 of a raw `Uint8Array` of 0/1, one byte per tile. Encode in chunks so
`String.fromCharCode(...)` never exceeds its argument limit.

Version is a hard requirement. Bump it on any breaking schema change and refuse to load a
mismatched version rather than guessing.

### 3. Round trip

```ts
export function serialize(state: GameState): SaveFile
export function deserialize(save: SaveFile): GameState
```

`deserialize` must: regenerate the level with the saved `generator` and `attempt`, then restore
every mutable field, then `restoreGameplayState(save.playRngState)`.

Order matters. Regeneration consumes the global RNG only, so the play RNG is untouched by it —
but restore it *after* regeneration so a future change to construction can never disturb it.

### 4. Triggers (DESIGN.md §8.3)

| Event | Action |
|---|---|
| Descending into a new level | Write — **after** construction, **before** any gameplay RNG use |
| Explicit quit from the pause menu | Write |
| Player death | **Delete** — permadeath |
| App start | If the save exists, offer **Continue** on the main menu |

No per-turn saves. Quitting mid-level resumes from the last checkpoint, not the last keystroke,
and `turnCount` reflects that honestly rather than pretending otherwise.

The level-entry write is the subtle one: it must capture `playRngState` at the moment the new
level begins, which is before the player has spent a single roll on it.

### 5. Run history (DESIGN.md §8.4)

On death or victory, append `{ seed, level, turns, kills, cause, won, endedAt }` to
`netdev_history_v1`, newest first, capped at 50.

## Tests — `test/save.test.ts`

- [ ] `serialize → deserialize` round-trips to a deep-equal `GameState` on 50 random runs
- [ ] The regenerated `tiles` are byte-identical to the original's
- [ ] `playRngState` survives the round-trip exactly, and the 100 draws following a
      save/load equal the 100 draws that would have followed without it
- [ ] Saving at level entry and reloading produces the identical level — same rooms, same
      enemies, same enemy positions, same items
- [ ] `explored` round-trips exactly, including an all-zero bitmap and a fully explored one
- [ ] Base64 encoding of a 1500-byte array survives the chunking boundary (test 0, 1, 8191, and
      1500 bytes)
- [ ] A `version` mismatch is rejected rather than loaded
- [ ] Malformed JSON in the save slot is caught and treated as "no save", not a crash
- [ ] `explored` with a non-`60 * 25` length is rejected
- [ ] Death deletes the save slot, and `hasSave()` returns `false` afterwards
- [ ] History is capped at 50 and ordered newest-first
- [ ] History survives death; the save slot does not
- [ ] Two runs of the same seed produce identical saves at the same turn count
- [ ] A save containing a `uniform` level restores to the same uniform level

## Done when

- [ ] `test/save.test.ts` green
- [ ] Reloading mid-run restores the same level, the same enemy positions, and the same
      `playRngState`
- [ ] `npm run verify` exits 0
